plan.title: Compressor and pneumatic muscle
plan.objective: Show compressor pressure feedback and mutually exclusive muscle fill and vent paths.
plan.rationale: A planar flow diagram separates air lines from control feedback.
interactions: Zoom and pan to inspect; fit restores full view
accessibilityRequirements: Labelled controls and SVG; keyboard pan

manifest.title: Compressor and pneumatic muscle
manifest.description: Air supply and pressure feedback with alternate fill and exhaust paths.
manifest.accessibilityDescription: Compressor pump feeds tank and regulator. Tank pressure controls a switch which turns the motor on and off. Regulated air feeds a valve connected to a muscle and room exhaust.

assumptions: Functional schematic; fill and vent arrows represent alternate states of the same muscle connection.
limitations: Does not specify fittings, pressure ratings, or safety equipment.

semanticTests.name: Compressor membership
semanticTests.assertion: Motor and air pump, tank, regulator and gauge, and pressure switch are within purchased compressor boundary.

semanticTests.name: Feedback direction
semanticTests.assertion: Tank-pressure signal runs from tank to switch; motor on/off control runs from switch to motor and air pump.

semanticTests.name: Air direction
semanticTests.assertion: Pump feeds tank, tank feeds regulator, regulator feeds valve; fill goes valve to muscle, release goes muscle to valve, exhaust goes valve to room.

semanticTests.name: Alternative states
semanticTests.assertion: Visible note states fill and vent are mutually exclusive and depicts two directions on the same muscle connection, not two simultaneously open lines.

semanticTests.name: Visual integrity
semanticTests.assertion: All edge endpoints derive from node ports; group contains its nodes; labels do not overlap nodes or each other, all contents are within initial bounds, and theme tokens maintain contrast.

files.index.html:
Compressor and pneumatic muscle

Drag to pan · Arrow keys to move

Alternative valve states: Fill: supply → muscle; exhaust closed. Vent: muscle → room; supply closed. Never simultaneously open.

Solid arrows: air flow. Dashed arrows: pressure sensing / motor control. Two muscle arrows show alternate flow directions through the same connection.
